newsitem.title: DENMARK: Banks push Danish shares to new record high.
newsitem.headline: Banks push Danish shares to new record high.

text.p: Danish share prices scaled new heights on Wednesday with activity, centred on bank shares, expected to continue on Thursday. Unidanmark reported lower than expected 1996 profits on Wednesday and Den Danske Bank DDBc.CO is to report on Thursday.

"The Unidanmark accounts were something of a disappointment, the share traded up before the report but fell after it was published. It was particularly foreign investors who sold out, disappointed at the unchanged dividend," a dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index rose 1.17 point to 158.71, in overall bourse turnover of 1.66 billion crowns.
The KFX March future rose 1.05 point to 158.25, with 1,472 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Unidanmark's report sent its share swinging between a high of 363 crowns and a low of 348 but it finished the day back at Tuesday's closing 355 crowns.
Den Danske Bank soared 37 crowns to 617, despite analysts' expectations that it would also report a drop in profits.
"Apparently nothing can stop the market rising at the moment and it will most probably go higher tomorrow," the dealer said.
BG Bank, due to report on February 24, was least affected, edging up three crowns to 304.
